desc: Formalize the greedy invariant: dangling length is forced to be subtree_size mod K; at each node at most 2 child chains can be absorbed (node is a single vertex), making the algorithm fully deterministic — no pairing/matching subproblem exists.
Handle special cases: K=1 works naturally (1%K=0 for every node → Yes); N=1 handled by general algorithm; K=2 reduces to perfect matching check, consistent with algorithm behavior.
Decide the exact combining rule at each node (replaces the multiset pairing task): ≥3 nonzero child danglings → No; 2 → s=a+b+1, No if s>K else d=s%K; 1 → d=(a+1)%K; 0 → d=1%K.
At the root, answer Yes iff no failure and root's returned d == 0.

Implement iterative post-order DFS (avoid recursion limits for NK up to 2·10^5): build adjacency list, compute parent/order via explicit stack, process nodes in reverse order, propagate dangling lengths with a global fail flag.
Write final Python solution with fast I/O (sys.stdin.buffer.read) and verify mentally against both samples plus edge cases (star, long path, NK=1, K=1).
